entries.title: Psalms 65:4
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Approach - To draw near to God in his house and ordinance, by prayer and praise, and other acts of communion with him. Satisfied - With the blessings there conferred upon thy people, the favour and fellowship of God, remission of sins, renovation of heart and life, joy and peace, and well - grounded assurance of eternal life.

entries.title: Psalms 65:5
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Righteousness - By virtue of thy faithfulness, and goodness. Wilt thou - Thou wilt graciously answer our prayers. The confidence - Thou art the stay and support of all mankind, by thy powerful and gracious providence.

entries.title: Psalms 65:8
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Thy tokens - Terrible thunders and lightnings, and earthquakes, and comets or other strange meteors, or works of God in the air. Morning - The successive courses of the morning and evening; or of the sun and moon which go forth at those times. Thus the whole verse speaks of the natural works of God, the former clause, of such as are extraordinary and terrible, the latter of such as are ordinary and delightful.

entries.title: Psalms 65:9
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: River - With rain, which he very significantly calls a river for its plenty, and the river of God, of God's immediate providing. Them - The inhabitants of the earth. Provided - Or, disposed, the earth, which without this would be hard and barren.

entries.title: Psalms 65:10
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Bringest down - For the rain dissolves the high and hard clods of earth.

entries.title: Psalms 65:12
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Wilderness - Which though neglected by men, are furnished with food for beasts.

entries.title: Psalms 65:13
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Sing - They are abundantly satisfied with thy goodness, and in their manner sing forth the praise of their benefactor.
